note.text:
Each piece of equipment has a job.
• Test tube: holds small amounts for reactions.
• Beaker: holds and heats liquids (its marks are rough).
• Conical flask: holds liquids that are swirled.
• Measuring cylinder: measures volumes of liquids.
• Burette: lets out an exact volume, drop by drop.
• Pipette: transfers one exact volume, such as 25 cm³.
• Dropper: adds a few drops.
• Gas jar: collects a gas.
• Watch glass: holds a little solid or evaporates a few drops.
Use the right equipment, keep it clean, and handle glass with care.

worked_example.problem: Bih needs exactly {v} cm³ of a solution for an experiment. Should she use a beaker, a measuring cylinder or a pipette?
steps: A beaker's marks are only rough.
A measuring cylinder is good, but not exact.
A pipette transfers one exact, fixed volume.

cards.idea: Containers: a test tube for small reactions, a beaker to hold and heat liquids, a conical flask to swirl liquids, a gas jar to collect a gas.
example: Mix two solutions in a test tube to see if they react.

cards.idea: Measuring volume: a measuring cylinder for most volumes; a pipette or burette when the volume must be exact.
example: A burette lets out the liquid drop by drop.

cards.idea: Handle glassware with care: carry it with both hands, never heat a measuring cylinder, and report breakages.
example: A measuring cylinder can crack in a flame: heat liquids in a beaker or test tube.

check.prompt: Which of these should NOT be heated?

wrong.explain: Beakers can be heated, on a tripod and gauze.
Test tubes can be heated, held with a test-tube holder.
Evaporating dishes are made to be heated.
